body:
_Original comment by_ **Torsten Marek (BitBucket: [tmarek](http://bitbucket.org/tmarek), GitHub: @tmarek?)**:

---

Is printing a warning acceptable, or do you want to have it silently accepted?

_Original comment by_ **Sylvain Thénault (BitBucket: [sthenault](http://bitbucket.org/sthenault), GitHub: @sthenault?)**:

---

This option  has been removed since it was very hard to provide bw compat for it using the new template system. If adding the option back and simply ignoring it sounds good to you, that's fairly easy, though I'm afraid such plugins will then fail on attempt to parse the output which won't be formatted as expected.

_Original comment by_ **Torsten Marek (BitBucket: [tmarek](http://bitbucket.org/tmarek), GitHub: @tmarek?)**:

---

I don't think this is a request for b/w compatibility, just not crashing and (silently?) ignoring the option.

_Original comment by_ **Kelly Schoenhofen (BitBucket: [kschoenhofen](http://bitbucket.org/kschoenhofen))**:

---

If you need to remove the feature, I totally understand. Don't put it back because one vocal user asked - I just need it to not error on the -i, and pass a warning/informational text. 

So yes, if you can put -i back and emit a warning (and not actually do -i) I would be more than happy, thank you very much. 

If the plugin needs the -i output format to parse the data, that's a different issue I can take up with the plugin authors. Thanks!

_Original comment by_ **Sylvain Thénault (BitBucket: [sthenault](http://bitbucket.org/sthenault), GitHub: @sthenault?)**:

---

Add back the -i and -s options for backwards compat, but have them be ignored.

Closes #180

_Original comment by_ **Sylvain Thénault (BitBucket: [sthenault](http://bitbucket.org/sthenault), GitHub: @sthenault?)**:

---

Removing version: 1.1 (automated comment)
